title.title: The generalized Mukai conjecture for Fano manifolds
title.subtitle: Claim: every Fano manifold has $\rho(\iota-1) \le n$, with equality only for $(\mathbb{P}^{\iota-1})^\rho$

plain: Shapes whose curves are all 'heavy' have room for only a few independent directions

beats.text: Heavy rational curves leave room for only a few independent directions
Products of projective spaces sit exactly on the bound

steps: Get lower bounds on counts of curves through a point
Turn them into $\rho$ independent eigenvalues of quantum multiplication

achievement.label: Generalized Mukai conjecture (2003)
achievement.context: Before: known up to dimension 5, for toric Fano manifolds and for large pseudoindex
achievement.note: A short Gromov–Witten proof, 19 pages, unrefereed

verify.detail: No Lean; the proof runs through eigenvalues of quantum multiplication
verify.ourCheck: We read the claim and caveats; we did not check the proof

voice.text: For a Fano manifold, rho times iota minus one is at most its dimension.
Curve counts through a point give rho eigenvalues of quantum multiplication, forcing the bound.
Claimed: true for every smooth Fano manifold.

sources.quote: It was known up to dimension 5.
The proof is a 19-page Gromov–Witten argument
